sophie: FYI rolled mixed-FP8 to dedicated-gpu pool at 09:12 — quick eval run shows regression on structured-output tests (JSON/table). hallucination rate +2.3% on JSON schemas, BLEU -1.7 on table gen. KV-cache miss rate spiked for long sequences (>1024). attaching traces and a couple logs below.

ajay: can you paste the eval summary + the minimal repro prompt? which model variant and quant config did we ship?

sophie: model=redwood-open-7b:fp8-mix-v1 (default kernel policy). eval-bot output below:

eval-bot: ```
run_id: canary-2026-02-18-09
model: redwood-open-7b:fp8-mix-v1
metrics:
  json_hall_rate: baseline=0.012, current=0.035, delta=+0.023
  BLEU_table: baseline=38.1, current=36.4, delta=-1.7
  avg_latency_p95: baseline=210ms, current=225ms
notes: failures concentrated on long context tests and structured-output prompts.
```

tim: profiler / perf trace shows repeated kernel fallback on QKV matmul when seq_len>1024 — runtime is selecting a low-precision fallback kernel path that doesn't use the prefix/KV tiled cache properly, causing recompute + cache misses. trace snippet:

```
# perf trace excerpt (summarized)
[09:13:04] attn_qkv_fp8_kernel_v1 -> fallback to int8_qkv_tiled_slow
[09:13:04] kv_cache: alloc miss, rebuilding tile for layer 10..23
[09:13:04] extra_matmul_recompute x3 for tokens 1024..1536
```

maria: the rollout config that went live:

```
-- rollout: canary
-- pool: dedicated-gpu-pool-3
-- kernel_policy: "auto_fp8_mixed"
-- calibration: per_layer_adaptive (enabled)
-- attn_threshold_seq_len: 1024
```

ajay: possible hypotheses: (1) per-layer calibration changed dynamic range for certain layers and made fp8 kernels trigger fallback more often; (2) kernel selector heuristic prefers fp8 impl that doesn't support tiled KV for long sequences; (3) batching heuristic/continuous batching increased effective seq_len due to prefix merging.

ajay: repro steps I want to try locally:
1) run eval harness with kernel_policy=force_fp8_attn_v2
2) same with kernel_policy=force_int8_attn_tiled
3) disable per_layer_adaptive calibration and use static calibration table

sophie: ran 1) and 2) on canary node: forcing fp8_attn_v2 reduced hallucination delta to +0.008 but p95 latency went up ~8%. forcing int8_tiled removed hallucination regression but BLEU stayed slightly down (-0.6). logs:

```
# canary run results
force_fp8_attn_v2: json_hall_rate=0.02, BLEU_table=37.8, p95=243ms
force_int8_tiled: json_hall_rate=0.014, BLEU_table=37.5, p95=217ms
auto_fp8_mixed: json_hall_rate=0.035, BLEU_table=36.4, p95=225ms
```

tim: that matches the kernel-selector theory. forcing the fp8_attn_v2 avoids fallback but it's heavier per-token (hence latency). int8_tiled keeps tiled KV benefits — explains lower p95.

maria: ops note — calibration pipeline did push new per-layer scales at 08:58, applied to canary at 09:10. I'm going to snapshot the calibration table and roll back to yesterday's table for a quick A/B.

infra-bot: deploy: rollback-calibration-table triggered for canary pool by maria at 09:28. will schedule a canary re-run. :gear:

eval-bot: canary re-run complete (09:34): json_hall_rate=0.013, BLEU_table=37.9, p95=218ms — looks much closer to baseline.

kevin: please file a regression + perf ticket with traces, eval diffs, and the calibration artifacts. we need an action item list:
- revert or pin calibration until kernel selector updated
- add a selector check to prefer tiled-KV-capable kernels when seq_len > attn_threshold
- add unit eval for structured JSON outputs in the canary gating
- perf/infra to benchmark fp8_attn_v2 latency tradeoffs

sophie: creating issue now: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RI-12458 (attached traces, eval CSVs, canary config). Plan: pin yesterday's calibration for canary/dedicated, add kernel-selector guard, and re-run full regression suite.

ajay: thumbs up. next steps: follow-up PR to runtime/kernel selector + a regression test added to eval harness. assign to tim + perf.

sophie: thanks all. I'll monitor canary and post updates here. :eyes:
